questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area in square units of the region bounded by the curve $y = \sqrt{16 - x^2}$ and lines $x = 0, x = 4$ above the X-axis is
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = \sqrt{16 - x^2}$, which represents the upper half of the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ with center $(0,0)$ and radius $4$.

The region bounded by the curve, $x = 0$, $x = 4$, and above the X-axis lies entirely in the first quadrant.

The required area is given by the integral:

$A = \int_{0}^{4} \sqrt{16 - x^2} dx$

Using the standard integral formula $\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1} \left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right), we get:

$ A = $\left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} +8\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right) \right]_{0}^{4}

$ A = $\left( 0 + 8\sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left(0 + 8\sin^{-1}(0) \right)$

$A = 8 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} ==4\pisq. units.

Answer: 4\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curves $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = -|x| + 1$ is
questions.solution:
The given curves are $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = -|x| + 1$.

To find the points of intersection, we equate the two equations:

$|x| - 1 = -|x| + 1$

$2|x| = 2 \Rightarrow |x| = 1 \Rightarrow x = \pm 1$

The required area $A$ is the region bounded between these two curves from $x = -1$ to $x = 1$.

$A = \int_{-1}^{1} [(-|x| + 1) - (|x| - 1)] dx$

$A = \int_{-1}^{1} (2 - 2|x|) dx$

Since the integrand is an even function:

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{1} (2 - 2x) dx$

$A = 2 \left[ 2x - x^2 \right]_{0}^{1}$

$A = 2 (2 - 1) = 2$ sq. units.

Answer: $2$ sq. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region lying in the first quadrant and bounded by the curve $y = 4x^2$, the Y-axis, and the lines $y = 2$, $y = 4$ is...
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = 4x^2$.

In the first quadrant, $x = \dfrac{\sqrt{y}}{2}$.

The required area is bounded by the curve, the Y-axis, and the lines $y = 2 and y = 4$.

Area $= \int_{2}^{4} x \, dy$

Area $= \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{\sqrt{y}}{2} \, dy$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{y^{3/2}}{3/2} \right]_{2}^{4}

Area $= $\dfrac{1}{3} \left[4^{3/2} - 2^{3/2} \right]$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[ 8 - 2\sqrt{2} \right] sq. units.

Answer: \dfrac{1}{3} \left[8 - 2\sqrt{2}\right] sq. units$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in square units) of the region bounded by the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 9$ and the parabola $y^2 \leq 8x$ is...
questions.solution:
To find the points of intersection of the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 9$ and the parabola $y^2 = 8x$, substitute $y^2 = 8x$ into the equation of the circle:

$x^2 + 8x - 9 = 0$

$(x + 9)(x - 1) = 0$

Since $x \geq 0$ for the parabola, we get $x = 1$.

The required region is bounded by $x^2 + y^2 \leq 9$ and $y^2 \leq 8x$. This region is symmetric with respect to the x-axis. The total area A$ is given by:

A = 2 \left( \int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{8x}$\, dx + \int_{1}^{3} $\sqrt{9 - x^2}$\, dx \right)$

Evaluating the first integral:

\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{8x}$\, dx = $2\sqrt{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3}$ x^{3/2} \right]_{0}^{1} = $\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{1}^{3} \sqrt{9 - x^2}$\, dx = \left[ $$\dfrac{x}{2}$ \sqrt{9 - x^2} + $\dfrac{9}{2} \sin^{-1}$$\left( $$\dfrac{x}{3}$ \right) \right]_{1}^{3}$$

Substituting the limits:

$= \left(0 + \dfrac{9}{2} \sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{8} + \dfrac{9}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right) \right)$

$= \dfrac{9\pi}{4} - \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{9}{2} \sin^{-1}\left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right)$

Adding the two integrals and multiplying by 2:

A = 2 $\left( \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} + \dfrac{9\pi}{4} - \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{9}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right) \right)

A = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3} + \dfrac{9\pi}{2} -2\sqrt{2} -9\sin^{-1} \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3} + \dfrac{9\pi}{2} -2\sqrt{2} -9\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region bounded by the curve $y = 2x - x^2$ and the X-axis is...
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = 2x - x^2$.

To find the points of intersection with the X-axis, set $y = 0$:

$2x - x^2 = 0$

$x(2 - x) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, x = 2$

The required area is the integral of the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:

$A = \int_{0}^{2} (2x - x^2) dx$

$A = \left[ x^2 - \dfrac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = \left( 2^2 - \dfrac{2^3}{3} \right) - 0$

$A = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ sq. units.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region enclosed by $\{(x, y) \mid y \leq x^2, xy \leq 8, y \geq 1\}$ is...
questions.solution:
The region is bounded by the curves $y = x^2$, $xy = 8$, and $y = 1$ in the first quadrant (as the area must be finite).

To find the intersection points of the curves:
Intersection of $y = x^2$ and $xy = 8$:
$x(x^2) = 8 \Rightarrow x^3 = 8 \Rightarrow x = 2$
At $x = 2$, $y = 4$.

Intersection of $y = x^2$ and $y = 1$:
$x^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1$ (taking $x > 0$).

Intersection of $xy = 8$ and $y = 1$:
$x(1) = 8 \Rightarrow x = 8$.

The area can be calculated by integrating with respect to $y$ from $y = 1$ to $y = 4$. For a given $y$, the value of $x$ ranges from the parabola $x = \sqrt{y}$ to the hyperbola $x = \dfrac{8}{y}$.

Required Area $= \displaystyle \int_{1}^{4} \left( \dfrac{8}{y} - \sqrt{y} \right) dy$

$= \left[ 8 \log y - \dfrac{2}{3} y^{3/2} \right]_{1}^{4}$

$= \left(8 \log 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} (4)^{3/2} \right) - \left(8 \log 1 - \dfrac{2}{3} (1)^{3/2} \right)$

$= \left(16 \log 2 - \dfrac{2}{3} (8) \right) - \left(0 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$

$= 16 \log 2 - \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$= 16 \log 2 - \dfrac{14}{3}$

Answer: $16\log 2 - \dfrac{14}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 4kx$ and the line $x = k$, (where $k > 0$) is $\dfrac{128}{3}$ sq. units, then the value of $\sin^{-1}  \left(\dfrac{2}{k}\right)is equal to...$
questions.solution:
The area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 4kx$ and the line $x = k$ is given by

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{k} y \, dx$

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{k} \sqrt{4kx} \, dx$

$A = 4\sqrt{k} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} x^{3/2} \right]_{0}^{k}$

$A = \dfrac{8}{3} k^2$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{128}{3}$, we have

$\dfrac{8}{3} k^2 = \dfrac{128}{3}$

$k^2 = 16$

Since $k > 0$, we get $k = 4$.

Substituting $k = 4$:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{k}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area bounded by $y = x^3 + ax$ (where $a > 0$), the $x$-axis and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 1$ is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units, then $\ldots$
questions.solution:
Given the curve $y = x^3 + ax$ with $a > 0$, the roots of $y = 0$ are given by $x(x^2 + a) = 0$. Since $a > 0$, the only real root is $x = 0$.

For $x \in [-2, 0]$, $y \le 0$, and for $x \in [0, 1]$, $y \ge 0$.

The required area $A$ is given by:

$A = \int_{-2}^{0} -(x^3 + ax) dx + \int_{0}^{1} (x^3 + ax) dx$

$A = -\left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{-2}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1}$

$A = -\left( 0 - \left( \dfrac{16}{4} + \dfrac{4a}{2} \right) \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} -0\right)$

$A = (4 + 2a) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units:

$\dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{37}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{20}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = 5 \Rightarrow a = 2$

Answer: $a = 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in square units) bounded by the line $y = x$, the X-axis and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 4$ is...
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the integral of $|y|$ with respect to $x$ from $x = -2$ to $x = 4$.

$A = \int_{-2}^{4} |x| dx$

$A = \int_{-2}^{0} (-x) dx + \int_{0}^{4} x dx$

$A = \left[ -\dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{-2}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left(0 - \left(-\dfrac{4}{2}\right)\right) + \left(\dfrac{16}{2} - 0\right)$

$A = 2 + 8 = 10$

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by curves $y = \sin x, y = \cos x$ and the lines $x = 0$, $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve between the given limits.

In the interval $x \in [0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}]$, $\cos x \ge \sin x$.

Area $= \int_{0}^{\pi/4} (\cos x - \sin x) dx$

$= [\sin x + \cos x]_{0}^{\pi/4}$

$= (\sin \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \cos \dfrac{\pi}{4}) - (\sin 0 + \cos 0)$

$= (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}) - (0 + 1)$

$= \sqrt{2} - 1$

Answer: $\sqrt{2} -$1

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Area enclosed by curve $y = 2x^2$ and lines $x \geq 1,\ y \leq 4$ is..... sq. units
questions.solution:
The region is bounded by the curve $y = 2x^2$, the vertical line $x = 1$, and the horizontal line $y = 4$.

The intersection of $y = 2x^2$ and $y = 4$ in the region $x \geq 1$ is given by:

$2x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x^2 = 2 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{2}$

The required area $A$ is the integral of the upper boundary minus the lower boundary from $x = 1$ to $x = \sqrt{2}$:

$A = \int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} (4 - 2x^2) dx$

$A = \left[ 4x - \dfrac{2x^3}{3} \right]_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}$

$A = \left( 4\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} \right) - \left( 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3} - \dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2} - 10}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}-10}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the lines $2x - y + 1 = 0,\ y = -1,\ y = 3$ and the y-axis is _____
questions.solution:
The given line is $2x - y + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{y - 1}{2}$

The required area is bounded by the curve $x = \dfrac{y - 1}{2}$, the y-axis ($x = 0$), and the lines $y = -1$ and $y = 3$.

Area $= \int_{-1}^{3} |x| dy = \int_{-1}^{3} \left| \dfrac{y - 1}{2} \right| dy$

Since $\dfrac{y - 1}{2} \le 0$ for $y \in [-1, 1]$ and $\dfrac{y - 1}{2} \ge 0$ for $y \in [1, 3]$:

Area $= \int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{1 - y}{2} dy + \int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{y - 1}{2} dy$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \left[ y - \dfrac{y^2}{2} \right]_{-1}^{1} + \dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{y^2}{2} - y \right]_{1}^{3}$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} \right) - \left( -1 - \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \right) + \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\left( \dfrac{9}{2} -3\right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{2} -1\right) \right)$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left( \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} \right) + \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right)$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} (2) + \dfrac{1}{2} (2) = 1 + 1 = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region common to the parabolas $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$ is...
questions.solution:
The given equations of the parabolas are $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$.

From the second equation, we have $y = \dfrac{3x^2}{16}$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$4\left(\dfrac{3x^2}{16}\right)^2 = 9x$

$\dfrac{9x^4}{64} = 9x$

$x^4 - 64x = 0$

$x(x^3 - 64) = 0$

The real roots are $x = 0$ and $x = 4$.

The required area $A$ is the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$:

$A = \int_{0}^{4} \left( \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{3x^2}{16} \right) dx$

$A = \left[ x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^3}{16} \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left( 4^{3/2} - \dfrac{4^3}{16} \right) - 0$

$A = 8 - 4 = 4$ sq. units.

Answer: 4 sq. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region enclosed by the lines $y = 2x, 2y = x$ and $x = 2$ (in sq.units) is...
questions.solution:
The given lines are $y = 2x$, $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$, and $x = 2$.

The points of intersection of the lines are $(0,0)$, $(2,4)$, and $(2,1)$.

The region is bounded by the upper line $y = 2x$ and the lower line $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$.

The area of the region is given by the integral of the difference between the upper and lower curves:

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \left(2x - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx$

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{3x}{2} dx$

$\text{Area} = \left[ \dfrac{3x^2}{4} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{3(2)^2}{4} - 0 = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $y = |x - 4|$, $x = 3$ and $x = 5$, and the X-axis is
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the definite integral of the function $y = |x - 4|$ from $x = 3$ to $x = 5$.

Area $= \int_{3}^{5} |x - 4| dx$

Since $|x - 4| = -(x - 4)$ for $x < 4$ and $|x - 4| = x - 4$ for $x \geq 4$, we split the integral at $x = 4$:

Area $= \int_{3}^{4} (4 - x) dx + \int_{4}^{5} (x - 4) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{3}^{4} (4 - x) dx = \left[ 4x - \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{3}^{4} = \left( 16 - \dfrac{16}{2} \right) - \left( 12 - \dfrac{9}{2} \right) = 8 - \dfrac{15}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{4}^{5} (x - 4) dx = \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} - 4x \right]_{4}^{5} = \left( \dfrac{25}{2} - 20 \right) - \left( \dfrac{16}{2} - 16 \right) = -\dfrac{15}{2} - (-8) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Total Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$ sq. unit.

Answer: $1$ sq. unit

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area bounded by the curve $x^2 = by$ and the lines $y = 1, y = 4$ in the first quadrant is $28$ sq. units, then the value of b is...
questions.solution:
The equation of the curve is $x^2 = by$. In the first quadrant, $x = \sqrt{b}\sqrt{y}$.

The area bounded by the curve and the lines $y = 1$ and $y = 4$ in the first quadrant is given by:

$\int_{1}^{4} x \, dy = 28$

$\int_{1}^{4} \sqrt{b}\sqrt{y} \, dy = 28$

$\sqrt{b} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} y^{3/2} \right]_{1}^{4} = 28$

$\dfrac{2}{3} \sqrt{b} (4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}) = 28$

$\dfrac{2}{3} \sqrt{b} (8 - 1) = 28$

$\dfrac{14}{3} \sqrt{b} = 28$

$\sqrt{b} = 28 \times \dfrac{3}{14}$

$\sqrt{b} = 6$

$b = 36$

Answer: $36$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the smaller region bounded by the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ and the line $x = 1$ is...
questions.solution:
The equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 = 4$.

The area of the smaller region bounded by the circle and the line $x = 1$ is given by:

$A = 2 \int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} \, dx$

Using the standard integral formula $\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} \, dx = \dfrac{x}{2} \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2} \sin^{-1} \left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right), we get:

$ A = 2 $\left[ \dfrac{x}{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} +2 \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \right]_{1}^{2}

Substituting$ the limits:

A = 2 $\left[ \left(0 + 2 \sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{3} + 2 \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \right) \right]$

$A = 2 \left[2 \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} -2 \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) \right]

$ A = 2 $\left[ \pi - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right]$

$A = 2 \left[ \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \right]

$A = $\dfrac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y = x^3$ and the lines $y = 8$ and $x = 0$ is... square units.
questions.solution:
The required area is bounded by the curve $y = x^3$, the line $y = 8$, and the y-axis ($x = 0$).

The point of intersection of $y = x^3$ and $y = 8$ in the first quadrant is $x = 2$.

The area can be calculated by integrating with respect to $x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:

$A = \int_{0}^{2} (8 - x^3) dx$

$A = \left[ 8x - \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = 16 - \dfrac{16}{4}$

$A = 16 - 4 = 12$

Alternatively, integrating with respect to $y$ from $y = 0$ to $y = 8$:

$A = \int_{0}^{8} x dy = \int_{0}^{8} y^{1/3} dy$

$A = \left[ \dfrac{3}{4} y^{4/3} \right]_{0}^{8}$

$A = \dfrac{3}{4} (8^{4/3}) = \dfrac{3}{4} (16) = 12$

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y = 2^{kx}$ and $x = 0, x = 2$, in first quadrant is $\dfrac{2}{\log 2}$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.solution:
The area of the region is given by

$A = \int_{0}^{2} 2^{kx} dx$

$A = \left[ \dfrac{2^{kx}}{k \log 2} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = \dfrac{2^{2k} - 1}{k \log 2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{2}{\log 2}$:

$\dfrac{2^{2k} - 1}{k \log 2} = \dfrac{2}{\log 2}$

$2^{2k} - 1 = 2k$

Checking the given options, for $k = \dfrac{1}{2}$:

$2^{2(1/2)} - 1 = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$2 - 1 = 1$

This satisfies the equation, hence $k = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region (in sq.units) bounded by the curve $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$ and the X-axis is _____
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $y^2 = 4(1 - x^2) \Rightarrow x^2 + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$.

This represents an ellipse with semi-minor axis $a = 1$ and semi-major axis $b = 2$.

Since $y \ge 0$, the given curve represents the upper half of the ellipse.

The area of the complete ellipse is $\pi a b = \pi(1)(2) = 2\pi$.

Therefore, the area of the upper half of the ellipse is $\dfrac{1}{2}(2\pi) = \pi$.

Alternatively, the area can be found by integration:

Area $= \int_{-1}^{1} 2\sqrt{1 - x^2} dx$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x \right]_{-1}^{1}$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right] = \pi$ sq. units.

Answer: $\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area enclosed between the curves $y^2 = 4kx$ and $y = kx, k > 0$ is $\dfrac{2k}{3}$ sq. units then $k = $
questions.solution:
Intersection points of $y^2 = 4kx$ and $y = kx$ are obtained by substituting $y = kx$ into $y^2 = 4kx$.

$(kx)^2 = 4kx$

$k^2x^2 - 4kx = 0$

$kx(kx - 4) = 0$

Since $k > 0$, $x = 0$ or $x = \dfrac{4}{k}$.

The area enclosed between the curves is given by:

$A = \int_{0}^{4/k} (2\sqrt{kx} - kx) dx$

$A = \left[ \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{k} x^{3/2} - \dfrac{k}{2} x^2 \right]_{0}^{4/k}$

$A = \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{k} \left(\dfrac{4}{k}\right)^{3/2} - \dfrac{k}{2} \left(\dfrac{4}{k}\right)^2$

$A = \dfrac{32}{3k} - \dfrac{8}{k} = \dfrac{8}{3k}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{2k}{3}$ sq. units:

$\dfrac{8}{3k} = \dfrac{2k}{3}$

$2k^2 = 8$

$k^2 = 4$

Since $k > 0$, $k = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $y = x\left|\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right|$ and the X-axis between the lines $x = 0$ and $x = 4\pi$ (in square units), is....
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the integral:

$A = \int_{0}^{4\pi} x\left|\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right| dx$

Since $\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \ge 0$ for $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ and $\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \le 0$ for $x \in [2\pi, 4\pi]$, the integral can be split as:

$A = \int_{0}^{2\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx - \int_{2\pi}^{4\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx$

Using integration by parts:

$\int x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = x\left(-2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right) - \int 1 \cdot \left(-2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right) dx$

$= -2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = \left[-2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{0}^{2\pi} = (-4\pi(-1) + 0) - (0 + 0) = 4\pi$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{2\pi}^{4\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = \left[-2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{2\pi}^{4\pi} = (-8\pi(1) + 0) - (-4\pi(-1) + 0) = -8\pi - 4\pi = -12\pi$

Substituting these values back into the area expression:

$A = 4\pi - (-12\pi) = 16\pi$

Answer: $16\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^3 \sqrt{9 - x^2} dx = $
questions.solution:
Using the standard integral formula:

$\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1} \left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)

Applying$ the limits from0 to 3$ with $a = 3$:

$\int_0^3 $\sqrt{9 - x^2}$dx = $\left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{9 - x^2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) \right]_$0^3$

$= $\left( 0 + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left( 0 + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}(0) \right)$

$= \dfrac{9}{2} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0$

$= \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$

Alternatively, the integral represents the area of a quarter circle of radius $3$ in the first quadrant, which is $\dfrac{1}{4} \times \pi(3)^2 = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the shaded region is... sq.units.
questions.solution:
From the given figure, the shaded region is bounded by the curve $y = \sin x$ from $x = 2\pi to x = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$ and by the curve $y = \cos x$ from $x = \dfrac{9\pi}{4} to x = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}$.

The area $A$ of the shaded region is given by the sum of two definite integrals:

$A = \int_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} \sin x \, dx + \int_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} \cos x \, dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} \sin x \, dx = [-\cos x]_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} = -\cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right) - (-\cos(2\pi))$

$= -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - (-1) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} \cos x \, dx = [\sin x]_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} = \sin \left(\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right)

$= 1 - $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}

Adding$ the two areas:

A = $\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) =2 - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} =2 - \sqrt{2}

Answer: 2 - \sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2=27 x$ and the line $x=1$ is ______ sq.units.
questions.solution:
The parabola $y^2 = 27x$ opens to the right and is symmetric about the x-axis. The region bounded by this parabola and the line $x = 1$ extends from the vertex at $x = 0$ to the boundary line.

From the parabola equation, $y = \pm 3\sqrt{3}\sqrt{x}$. By symmetry, we compute the area as twice the area above the x-axis:

$A = 2\int_0^1 3\sqrt{3}\sqrt{x}dx = 6\sqrt{3}\int_0^1 x^{1/2}dx$

$A = 6\sqrt{3}\left[\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_0^1 = 6\sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 4\sqrt{3}$

The area is $4\sqrt{3}$ square units, corresponding to option C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $\mathrm{y}=|x-4|, x=3$ and $x=5$, and the X -axis is
questions.solution:
The area under $y=|x-4|$ between $x=3$ and $x=5$ is given by the integral $\int_{3}^{5} |x-4| dx$.

The absolute value function splits at $x=4$, requiring evaluation in two parts:

$\int_{3}^{5} |x-4| dx = \int_{3}^{4} (4-x) dx + \int_{4}^{5} (x-4) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{3}^{4} (4-x) dx = \left[4x - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{3}^{4} = (16 - 8) - (12 - 4.5) = 8 - 7.5 = 0.5$

The second integral yields:

$\int_{4}^{5} (x-4) dx = \left[\frac{x^2}{2} - 4x\right]_{4}^{5} = (12.5 - 20) - (8 - 16) = (-7.5) - (-8) = 0.5$

Summing both contributions gives the total area:
$0.5 + 0.5 = 1$

The area is 1 square unit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area bounded by the curve $x^2=4 \mathrm{y}$, X-axis and the line $x=4$ is divided into equal areas by the line $x=\alpha$, then the value of $\alpha$ is...
questions.solution:
The area under the curve $x^2 = 4y$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$ is found by integrating $y = \frac{x^2}{4}$ over this interval.

$A_{\text{total}} = \int_{0}^{4} \frac{x^2}{4} dx = \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{4} = \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{64}{3} = \frac{16}{3}$

The line $x = \alpha$ divides this region into two equal areas, so the area from $x = 0$ to $x = \alpha$ must be $\frac{8}{3}$.

$\int_{0}^{\alpha} \frac{x^2}{4} dx = \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{\alpha} = \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{\alpha^3}{12} = \frac{8}{3}$

Solving gives $\alpha^3 = 32 \implies \alpha = 32^{1/3}$, which corresponds to option D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of smaller part between the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ and the line $x=1$ is _______  sq.units.
questions.solution:
The area of the smaller segment bounded by the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ (radius $r = 2$) and the vertical line $x = 1$ can be determined using integration or geometry.

Using integration, the area is given by $A = 2 \int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} \, dx$. The standard antiderivative yields:

$A = 2 \left[ \frac{x}{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} + 2 \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{x}{2} \right) \right]_{1}^{2}$

Evaluating from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$ gives:

$A = 2 \left[ \left( 0 + 2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} \right) - \left( \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{3} + 2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right] = 2 \left( \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \right)$

Simplifying results in $A = \frac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$.

Geometrically, the intersections at $x = 1$ occur at $y = \pm \sqrt{3}$, forming a central angle of $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ radians. The sector area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{3}$, and the triangle area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{3} \cdot 1 = \sqrt{3}$. Subtracting gives the same result: $\frac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $\mathrm{y}=4 x-x^2$ and X - axis in square units, is $\qquad$
questions.solution:
The area bounded by $y = 4x - x^2$ and the X-axis is determined by finding the points of intersection. Setting $y = 0$ yields $4x - x^2 = 0 or x(4 - x) = 0$, so $x = 0 and x = 4$ serve as the limits of integration.

Between these limits, the parabola is above the X-axis since $y$ is positive. The area is thus given by the definite integral $\int_{0}^{4} (4x - x^2) dx$.

Evaluating the integral:

$\left[ 2x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{4} = \left(32 - \frac{64}{3}\right) - 0 = \frac{32}{3}$.

This matches option A.

Answer: A

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the parabolas $\mathrm{y}=9 x^2, \mathrm{y}=\frac{x^2}{16}$ and the line $\mathrm{y}=1$ is
questions.solution:
Given the parabolas $y = 9x^2$ and $y = \frac{x^2}{16}$ and the line $y = 1$, the area is determined by integrating with respect to $y$ due to the symmetry about the $y$-axis.

Solving for $x$ in terms of $y$ yields the right boundary $x = 4\sqrt{y}$ from $y = \frac{x^2}{16}$ and the left boundary $x = \frac{\sqrt{y}}{3}$ from $y = 9x^2$ in the first quadrant. The integral for half the area is $A_{half} = \int_0^1 \left( 4\sqrt{y} - \frac{\sqrt{y}}{3} \right) dy = \frac{11}{3} \int_0^1 \sqrt{y} dy$.

$\int_0^1 y^{1/2} dy = \left[ \frac{2}{3} y^{3/2} \right]_0^1 = \frac{2}{3}$
Thus, $A_{half} = \frac{11}{3} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = \frac{22}{9}$.

Due to symmetry, the total area is $2 \cdot \frac{22}{9} = \frac{44}{9}$ square units.

Answer: B

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $\mathrm{y}=x^2+3, \mathrm{y}=x, x=3$ and y -axis is...
questions.solution:
Area Between Curves

The area bounded by $y=x^2+3$, $y=x$, $x=3$, and $x=0$ is determined by the definite integral of the difference between the upper and lower functions over the interval $[0, 3]$.

Since $x^2+3 > x$ for all $x$ (as $x^2 - x + 3$ has discriminant $-11$ and is always positive), the area is computed as:

$A = \int_0^3 [(x^2+3) - x] dx = \int_0^3 (x^2 - x + 3) dx$

Evaluating the integral:

$A = \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{x^2}{2} + 3x \right]_0^3 = \left( \frac{27}{3} - \frac{9}{2} + 9 \right) - (0) = 9 - \frac{9}{2} + 9 = \frac{27}{2}$

The area is $\frac{27}{2}$ square units, corresponding to option C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $x^2=8 \mathrm{y}$ and the straight line $x-8 y+2=0$ is
questions.solution:
Area bounded by curve and line

Solving for $y$ in both equations: the parabola becomes $y = \frac{x^2}{8}$, and the line becomes $y = \frac{x+2}{8}$.

The intersection points are found by setting $\frac{x^2}{8} = \frac{x+2}{8}$, yielding $x^2 = x+2$ or $x^2 - x - 2 = 0$. Factoring gives $(x-2)(x+1)=0$, so $x = -1$ and $x = 2$ are the points of intersection.

At $x=0$, the line gives $y = \frac{1}{4}$ and the parabola gives $y=0$, so the line lies above the parabola on the interval $[-1,2]$.

The area is given by the integral of the difference:

$A = \int_{-1}^{2} \left( \frac{x+2}{8} - \frac{x^2}{8} \right) \, dx = \frac{1}{8} \int_{-1}^{2} (x+2 - x^2) \, dx$

Evaluating the integral:

$\frac{1}{8} \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} + 2x - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{-1}^{2} = \frac{1}{8} \left(\left(2+4-\frac{8}{3}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{2} -2 + \frac{1}{3}\right) \right)

$= $\frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{10}{3} + \frac{7}{6} \right) = \frac{1}{8} \cdot \frac{27}{6} = \frac{9}{16}

The area is \frac{9}{16}$sq. units, so the correct option is C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a curve $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{a} \sqrt{x}+\mathrm{b} x$ passes through the point $(1,2)$ and the area bounded by this curve, line $x=4$ and the X -axis is 8 sq.units, then the value of $a-b$ is
questions.solution:
Given the curve $y = a\sqrt{x} + bx$ passes through the point $(1, 2)$, substitution yields:

$2 = a + b$

The area bounded by the curve, line $x = 4$, and the X-axis is given by:

$\int_{0}^{4} (a\sqrt{x} + bx) dx = 8$

Evaluating the integral:

$\int_{0}^{4} (a\sqrt{x} + bx) dx = \left[\frac{2a}{3}x^{3/2} + \frac{b}{2}x^{2}\right]_{0}^{4} = \frac{16a}{3} + 8b$

Setting this equal to 8 and simplifying:

$\frac{16a}{3} + 8b = 8$

$2a + 3b = 3$

Solving the system $a + b = 2$ and $2a + 3b = 3$ gives $a = 3$, $b = -1$.

The required value is:

$a - b = 3 - (-1) = 4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $x=2-y-y^2$ and the $Y$-axis is
questions.solution:
The curve $x = 2 - y - y^2$ intersects the Y-axis when $x = 0$, giving $y^2 + y - 2 = 0$, which factors as $(y + 2)(y - 1) = 0$. The roots $y = -2 and y = 1$ determine the limits of integration.

Between these roots, $x = 2 - y - y^2$ remains positive, so the area is given directly by

$A = \int_{-2}^{1} (2 - y - y^2) \, dy$

Integrating term by term yields

$\left[2y - \frac{y^2}{2} - \frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{1}$

Evaluating at the bounds gives

$\left(2 - \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) - \left(-4 - \frac{4}{2} + \frac{8}{3}\right) = \frac{7}{6} - \left(-\frac{10}{3}\right) = \frac{7}{6} + \frac{20}{6} = \frac{27}{6} = \frac{9}{2}$

The area bounded by the curve and the Y-axis is $\frac{9}{2}$ square units.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $\mathrm{y}=|x-2|$ between $x=1, x=3$ and X -axis is......
questions.solution:
The area bounded by $y=|x-2|$ from $x=1$ to $x=3$ and the X-axis is found by evaluating $\int_{1}^{3} |x-2| dx$.

The piecewise definition of $|x-2|$ gives two subintervals: $[1,2]$ where $|x-2|=2-x$ and $[2,3]$ where $|x-2|=x-2$. The integral splits accordingly:

$\int_{1}^{3} |x-2| dx = \int_{1}^{2} (2-x) dx + \int_{2}^{3} (x-2) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{1}^{2} (2-x) dx = \left[2x - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{1}^{2} = (4-2) - \left(2 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 2 - \frac{3}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$

The second integral yields:

$\int_{2}^{3} (x-2) dx = \left[\frac{x^2}{2} - 2x\right]_{2}^{3} = \left(\frac{9}{2}-6\right) - \left(\frac{4}{2}-4\right) = -\frac{3}{2} + 2 = \frac{1}{2}$

The total area is $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1$ square unit.

Geometrically, the region comprises two congruent right triangles with bases and heights of length $1$ each, confirming the area of $1$ square unit.

The area is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area inside the parabola $y^2=4 a x$, between the lines $x=a$ and $x=4 a$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Area inside the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ between $x = a$ and $x = 4a$.

The parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ is symmetric about the x-axis, with the upper half given by $y = 2\sqrt{ax}$.

The total area is twice the area above the x-axis, so we compute $A = 2 \int_a^{4a} 2\sqrt{ax} dx = 4\sqrt{a} \int_a^{4a} \sqrt{x} dx$.

Evaluating the integral: $4\sqrt{a} \left[ \frac{2}{3} x^{3/2} \right]_a^{4a} = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \left( (4a)^{3/2} - a^{3/2} \right)$.

Simplifying: $(4a)^{3/2} = 8a^{3/2}$, so $A = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} (8a^{3/2} - a^{3/2}) = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \cdot 7a^{3/2} = \frac{56}{3} a^2$.

This corresponds to option C: $\frac{56a^2}{3}$ square units.

questions.q: AOB is the positive quadrant of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$ in which $\mathrm{OA}=5, \mathrm{OB}=3$. The area between the $\operatorname{arc} \mathrm{AB}$ and the chord AB of the ellipse in sq.units is
questions.solution:
The ellipse equation is $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$, so $a = 5$ and $b = 3$.

The quadrant area is $\frac{1}{4} \pi a b = \frac{15\pi}{4}$.

The right triangle OAB with vertices $(0,0)$, $(5,0)$, and $(0,3)$ has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 3 = \frac{15}{2}$.

The area between arc and chord AB is $\frac{15\pi}{4} - \frac{15}{2} = \frac{15(\pi - 2)}{4}$, matching option D.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1$ and the line $\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{2}=1$ is
questions.solution:
Area bounded by ellipse and line in first quadrant

The ellipse $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1$ has semi-axes $a=3$ and $b=2$, with x-intercept $(3,0)$ and y-intercept $(0,2)$.

The line $\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{2}=1$ passes through these same intercepts, forming a triangle with coordinate axes. The region bounded by the ellipse and line corresponds to the quarter-elliptical area in the first quadrant minus this triangular area.

The total elliptical area is $A_{ellipse} = \pi ab = \pi(3)(2) = 6\pi$, so the first quadrant portion is $\frac{6\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{2}$.

The triangle formed by the line and axes has area $A_{triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 2 = 3$.

The bounded area is therefore $\frac{3\pi}{2} - 3 = \frac{3}{2}(\pi - 2)$, matching option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area enclosed between the curves $\mathrm{y}^2=4 x$ and $\mathrm{y}=|x|$ is
questions.solution:
The curves $y^2=4x$ and $y=|x|$ intersect at $(0,0)$ and $(4,4)$, and their enclosed region lies in the first quadrant.

For $0 \leq x \leq 4$, the parabola gives $y = 2\sqrt{x}$ (upper curve) and $y = x$ (lower curve).

The area is $A = \int_{0}^{4} (2\sqrt{x} - x) \, dx = \left[ \frac{4}{3}x^{3/2} - \frac{1}{2}x^2 \right]_{0}^{4} = \left( \frac{4}{3}(8) - \frac{1}{2}(16) \right) = \frac{32}{3} - 8 = \frac{8}{3}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\frac{8}{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The ratio of the areas bounded by the curves $\mathrm{y}=\cos x$ and $\mathrm{y}=\cos 2 x$ between $x=0, x=\frac{\pi}{3}$ and X -axis is
questions.solution:
The ratio of areas bounded by $y = \cos x$ and $y = \cos 2x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ is determined by evaluating the respective definite integrals.

The area under $y = \cos x$ evaluates to $A_1 = \int_0^{\pi/3} \cos x\, dx = \sin x \Big|_0^{\pi/3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 0 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

For $y = \cos 2x$, the area is $A_2 = \int_0^{\pi/3} \cos 2x\, dx = \frac{1}{2} \sin 2x \Big|_0^{\pi/3} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 0 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$.

The ratio $A_1 : A_2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} : \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = 2 : 1$, which corresponds to option C.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region described by $\left\{(x, y) / y^2 \leq 2 x\right.$ and $\left.y \geq(4 x-1)\right\}$ is
questions.solution: Putting $x=\frac{y^2}{2}$ in y=4 x-1, we get $\begin{aligned} & y=4\left(\frac{y^2}{2}\right)-1 \Rightarrow 2 y^2-y-1=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(y-1)(2 y+1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=1, \frac{-1}{2} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Required area $\begin{aligned} & =\int_{-1 / 2}^1\left(\frac{y+1}{4}\right) \mathrm{d} y-\int_{-1 / 2}^1 \frac{y^2}{2} \mathrm{ d} y \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+y\right]_{-1 / 2}^1-\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1 / 2}^1 \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8}\right)+\left(1+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{24}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{9}{24}\right) \\ & =\frac{15}{32}-\frac{3}{16} \\ & =\frac{9}{32} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If two sides of a square are $4 x+3 y-20=0$ and $4 x+3 y+15=0$, then the area of the square is

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region $\left\{(x, y) / x \geq 0, x+y \leq 3, x^2 \leq 4 y\right.$ and $\left.y \leq 1+\sqrt{x}\right\}$ is
questions.solution: Given inequalities are $\begin{aligned} & x \geq 0 \\ & x+y \leq 3 \\ & x^2 \leq 4 y, \\ & y \leq 1+\sqrt{x} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ The equalities are $\begin{aligned} & x+y=3 ...(i)\\ & x^2=4 y ...(ii)\\ & y=1+\sqrt{x}...(iii) \end{aligned}$ from (i) and (iii), we get $\begin{array}{ll} & 3-x=1+\sqrt{x} \\ \therefore \quad & x+\sqrt{x}-2=0 \end{array} $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad$& ($\sqrt{x}+$2)($\sqrt{x}-$1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow $\sqrt{x}=$1 \quad \ldots[\because $\sqrt{x} \text{ cannot be negative }]$\\ & \Rightarrow x=1 $\text{ and }$y=2 \end{aligned}$ \\ From (i) and (ii), we get $$\begin{array}{ll}$& x+$\frac{x^2}{4}=$3 \\ \therefore \quad & x²+4 x-12=0 \\ \therefore \quad & (x+6)(x-2)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=2 \\ & \Rightarrow y=1 \end{array} $\ldots[\because x \geq 0]\therefore \quad$ Required area $\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^1\left(1+\sqrt{x}-\frac{x^2}{4}\right) \mathrm{d} x+\int_1^2\left(3-x-\frac{x^2}{4}\right) \mathrm{d} x \\ & =\int_0^1(1+\sqrt{x}) \mathrm{d} x+\int_1^2(3-x)-\frac{1}{4} \int_0^2 x^2 \mathrm{~d} x \\ & =[x]_0^1+\frac{2}{3}\left[x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right]_0^1+3[x]_1^2-\frac{1}{2}\left[x^2\right]_1^2-\frac{1}{12}\left[x^3\right]_0^2 \\ & =1+\frac{2}{3}+3-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{2}{3} \\ & =\frac{5}{2} \end{aligned}$
